unmapped_findings: The 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q condition was designed to reach minimum short-range ordering: quenching from 600 °C suppresses short-range ordering nearly completely, whereas maximum ordering requires a 250 °C/14 day anneal; nevertheless this minimum-order state gave the same hardness as the as-grown Fe-16%Al monocrystal (HU ~2000 N/mm²), so short-range order has no major impact on hardness.

For the [112]-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal the 1100 °C FC 600 °C Q compressive stress-strain curve (RT, 10^-4 s^-1) is essentially identical to the as-grown and furnace-cooled (to RT) curves; only quenching from 1100 °C followed by a 300 °C/14 day anneal produced a higher yield stress, i.e. only heat treatments above 600 °C significantly affect the mechanical behaviour.

In Fig. 1 this condition is labelled '1100°C FC600°CQ' (furnace cooling from 1100 °C down to 600 °C with subsequent water quench) and is also written as '1100 °C FC 600 °CQ'; no numeric HU value is printed in the figure, so ~2000 N/mm² is read against the 2000 N/mm² gridline.
